authority.legal_name: West Bengal Transport Corporation (WBTC), Government of West Bengal — Transport Department, operating the Hooghly River ferry network
authority.geography_type: the Hooghly (Ganga) river running through the Kolkata–Howrah metropolis and upriver to the heritage riverfront towns

mandate.summary: The West Bengal Transport Corporation runs the public ferry network on the Hooghly — the river crossings that move hundreds of thousands of commuters daily between Kolkata and Howrah and along the riverfront, taking pressure off the Howrah Bridge and the city's saturated roads. WBTC's mandate is affordable, reliable, and increasingly zero-emission public river transport for the metropolis.
current_priorities: Relieving road and bridge congestion with fast, frequent river crossings
Modernizing an ageing diesel ferry fleet to zero-emission electric vessels
Extending reliable public service along the Hooghly riverfront and to the heritage towns

policy_targets.interim_target: India's national net-zero-by-2070 commitment and West Bengal's active shift to battery-electric river ferries; the state is procuring a fleet of electric/hybrid vessels to decarbonize the Hooghly network
policy_targets.vision: A modern, zero-emission public ferry network on the Hooghly — faster crossings, cleaner air, and relief for one of India's most congested urban cores
policy_targets.relevance: West Bengal is already replacing diesel ferries with battery-electric vessels; a foiling-electric platform extends that program to fast, low-wake crossings that cut journey times on the busiest Kolkata–Howrah legs while eliminating emissions and wake erosion on a heavily-used river.

precedent.headline: West Bengal has already launched India's next-generation electric river ferry — this scales a live program.

existing_program.operator: WBTC (Government of West Bengal), vessels by GRSE and Cochin Shipyard
existing_program.program: 'Dheu' — a Next-Generation battery-electric catamaran ferry delivered January 2025 and operating on the Hooghly; 13 further hybrid-electric ferries under construction for the Government of West Bengal; backed by the World Bank-supported West Bengal Inland Water Transport, Logistics & Spatial Development program
existing_program.proof_stat: A live, government-run electric ferry already carrying passengers on the Hooghly — the platform a foiling fleet accelerates
existing_program.note: Public river-transport network; the mandate is congestion relief + decarbonization.

interpretation_for_navier: Anchor on the busiest Kolkata–Howrah commuter crossings (Howrah↔Millennium Park, Howrah↔Fairlie Place), then the northern riverfront (Fairlie Place↔Bagbazar; Dakshineswar↔Belur Math pilgrimage corridor), then the upriver heritage line-haul (Millennium Park↔Chandannagar). Geometry is ALREADY SEALED in the atlas — bind the real route_ids. Domestic-first; no cross-border link.

domestic_network.note: Real atlas boarding points (bp-<hash>) with real coordinates; real sealed routes (rn-<hash>) already exist in ROUTES.json — BIND them, do not null. Distances from the sealed atlas.

sealed_pairs.rationale: Howrah ↔ Fairlie Place — a core Kolkata–Howrah commuter crossing relieving Howrah Bridge road traffic.
Howrah ↔ Millennium Park — the busiest river crossing between Howrah station and central Kolkata's riverfront.
Fairlie Place ↔ Bagbazar — connecting the central ghats to the northern Kolkata riverfront.
Dakshineswar ↔ Belur Math — the pilgrimage crossing between two of the Hooghly's most-visited temple/monastery riverfronts.
Millennium Park ↔ Chandannagar — the upriver heritage-town line-haul, where foiling speed makes a scheduled connection viable.

regional_links.note: Domestic Hooghly network stands alone. No cross-border corridor.

routing_hazards.instruction: Route down the Hooghly channel to the charted ghats; respect strong tidal bore currents, heavy country-boat and barge traffic, and pontoon-jetty approaches. Provide explicit hand waypoints around the Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu) and Vidyasagar Setu piers.

hazards.detail: The Hooghly has powerful tidal currents and periodic bores; timing and current-aware routing to the ghats is essential.

hazards.hazard: Howrah Bridge / Vidyasagar Setu bridge piers
hazards.detail: Crossings pass under the Rabindra Setu (Howrah Bridge) and Vidyasagar Setu; route the charted navigation spans, clear of piers.

hazards.hazard: Dense country-boat, barge and ferry traffic
hazards.detail: The Kolkata–Howrah reach is congested with pontoon ferries, country boats and cargo barges; low-wake foiling helps but route defensively.
Heavy monsoon flow, shifting silt banks and floating pontoon jetties require careful, tide-aware berth approaches.
